s: Mother tongue of the Devagiri Yadavas?
x:
The Devagiri (Seuna) Yadavas ruled large parts of present-day Maharashtra between the 12th and 14th centuries with Devagiri (Daulatabad) as their capital. Their mother tongue was Marathi, and they greatly encouraged Marathi language and literature. Although Sanskrit continued to be the language of administration and scholarship, Marathi flourished under their patronage. The Yadava court patronized eminent scholars such as Hemadri and saint-poets like Dnyaneshwar, who composed the famous Dnyaneshwari in Marathi. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).

s: Who was the ruler of Devgiri at the time of Alauddin Khalji’s invasion?
x: Ramchandra Dev was the ruler of Devgiri at the time of Alauddin Khalji’s invasion. In 1296 A.D., the king of Devgiri, Ramchandra Dev after the successful invasion of Alauddin Khalji promised him to send the revenue from Ellichpur every year, but he did not send the tax to Delhi. Consequently, Alauddin sent an army under the leadership of Malik Kafur to attack Devgiri in 1307. King Ramchandra Dev was defeated and surrendered. Malik Kafur looted Devgiri and took Ramchandra Dev including his relatives to Delhi. Alauddin behaved with dignity with Ramchandra Dev and gave him the title of ‘Rai Rayan’ and sent him back to his state offering 1 lakh ‘Tankas’ and ‘Navsari’ district. Malik Kafur had also led a campaign against Shankar Dev, the son of Ramchandra in 1312 AD.

s: Kakatiyas were feudatories of which Andhra dynasty?
x:
The early Kakatiyas served as feudatories of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi before emerging as an independent power. The earliest Kakatiya chiefs such as Beta I and Prola I acknowledged the overlordship of the Eastern Chalukya rulers. As the power of the Eastern Chalukyas declined, the Kakatiyas gradually strengthened their position and eventually established an independent kingdom under Rudradeva with Warangal (Orugallu) as their capital. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Early Overlords – Eastern Chalukyas
• First Independent Kakatiya Ruler – Rudradeva

s: To whom were the Kakatiyas feudatories before establishing their independent kingdom?
x:
The early Kakatiyas first served as feudatories of the Rashtrakutas. After the decline of the Rashtrakutas, they became vassals of the Western Chalukyas of Kalyani. Later rulers such as Prola II and Rudradeva (Prataparudra I) asserted independence and laid the foundation for the powerful Kakatiya kingdom with Orugallu (Warangal) as its capital. Thus, the Kakatiyas rose gradually from feudatories to one of the greatest dynasties of medieval Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note: Chronology:
• Rashtrakutas → Western Chalukyas → Independent Kakatiyas

s: Who were the kings who had the title 'Mahamandaleswara'?
x:
The title "Mahamandaleswara" literally means "Great Lord of Provinces". During the early phase of their political career, the Kakatiya rulers, while serving as feudatories under the Western Chalukyas, frequently used this title. It denoted powerful provincial governors or feudatory chiefs controlling large territories. Even after attaining independence, the title continued to appear in several Kakatiya inscriptions as a mark of prestige and authority. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).

s: Who among the following was awarded the title 'Founder of Kakati Rajya'?
x:
Recherla Rudra was one of the most distinguished military commanders of the Kakatiya kingdom. After the death of Rudradeva, he played a crucial role in protecting the kingdom from external invasions and internal rebellions. During the captivity of Ganapatideva by the Yadavas, Recherla Rudra safeguarded the kingdom and later helped restore Kakatiya authority. For his immense contribution in strengthening and consolidating the Kakatiya kingdom, he was honored with the title "Kakati Rajya Sthapanacharya" (Founder/Restorer of the Kakatiya Kingdom). His services were instrumental in transforming the Kakatiyas into a powerful medieval empire. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).

s: What is another name for Motupalli?
x:
Motupalli was one of the most important medieval seaports of Andhra Pradesh. Historical records and literary works refer to it by another name, Deseeyakkonda Pattanam. During the Kakatiya and Reddi periods, Motupalli emerged as a flourishing international port with trade links to Sri Lanka, China, Southeast Asia, Arabia and Persia. Horses, pearls, spices, textiles and precious stones were among the important commodities traded through this port. The famous Motupalli Charter issued by Kakatiya Ganapatideva granted special commercial privileges and security to foreign merchants, encouraging overseas trade. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Motupalli = Deseeyakkonda Pattanam
• Famous for – Maritime Trade
• Important Charter – Motupalli Charter of Ganapatideva

s: The main port town of the Kakatiya period?
x:
Motupalli, situated on the Andhra coast, was the principal seaport of the Kakatiya Empire. It served as an important centre for overseas trade with Arabia, China and Southeast Asia. The famous Motupalli Charter (Abhaya Sasana) issued by Ganapatideva guaranteed protection and trading privileges to foreign merchants. Exports included textiles, diamonds, spices and horses, making Motupalli one of the busiest medieval ports in South India. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Main Kakatiya Port → Motupalli
• Famous inscription → Motupalli Abhaya Sasana

s: Which ruler issued the famous Motupalli Charter?
x:
Ganapatideva, one of the greatest rulers of the Kakatiya dynasty, issued the famous Motupalli Charter to encourage overseas trade. The charter granted commercial privileges, protection and tax concessions to foreign merchants visiting the port of Motupalli. It assured traders of safety and promoted maritime commerce with countries such as China, Sri Lanka, Arabia and Southeast Asia. The Motupalli Charter reflects the Kakatiyas' farsighted economic policy and highlights the importance of maritime trade in medieval Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Issued by – Ganapatideva
• Charter – Motupalli Charter
• Purpose – Promotion of Overseas Trade
